root.name: King's Indian Defense: Kramer Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nge2

overview: White develops the king's knight on e2 instead of f3, keeping the f-pawn free and planning Ng3, Be2 and O-O (or a quick f3/Be3 set-up). After 5...O-O 6.Ng3 e5 7.d5 the centre locks and the game becomes a King's Indian structure where White plays on the queenside with c5 or Be3 and Black pushes ...Na6, ...Nh5 and ...f5. It is quieter than the Mar del Plata and less theory-heavy, but Black still needs to time the f5 break correctly.

white_ideas.idea: Ng3, Be2, O-O and Be3 with a solid central set-up
Close the centre with d5 and play c5 or queenside space gains
Keep the f-pawn free for f3 and a flexible Be3/Qd2 attack

black_ideas.idea: Castle, play ...e5 and meet d5 with ...Na6 or ...Nbd7 and ...Nh5 to hit Ng3
Break with ...c6 if White locks the centre or keep ...exd4 options

typical_structures.structure: Locked King's Indian centre: White d5/e4/c4 against Black e5/d6, with play on opposite wings

character.notes: Less forcing than the Classical or Sämisch because the knight on e2/g3 slows White's own attack; no mutual race by force. Balanced, though King's Indian structures always carry some risk.

structure.notes: After 6.Ng3 e5 7.d5 the centre is locked and play moves to the wings. Closed.

approach.notes: A system-flavoured move order against the KID but it is not played against everything; standard.

level.notes: Plans and timing of ...f5 are the hard part, but the line is less forcing than the Mar del Plata; Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 6.Ng3 e5 7.d5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nge2 O-O 6. Ng3 e5 7. d5
sublines_that_differ.how: The main line; centre locks and play moves to the wings.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5...Nc6 6.Ng3
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nge2 Nc6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black pressures d4 early and steers towards an e5 break with more tension.

character.reason: A quieter White set-up than the Classical KID, though the locked centre still brings wing play and risk.

structure.reason: After ...e5 and d5 the centre locks, as in the King's Indian anchor.

approach.reason: It is a specific line against the KID, not a set-up for any defence.

level.reason: KID structures are demanding, but this branch is less forcing; could be read as Advanced.

plans.reason: White gains queenside space while Black storms the kingside with ...f5.
